### Problem description

MiniMax is currently in public testing period. It means that the focus currently is on making sure that:
- Its setup steps work without issues.
- Existing config provides an experience it is intended to provide.
- Documentation is understandable and doesn't contain factual/spelling mistakes.

Any feedback about any of the above is very welcome. Either here or in a separate issue.

What is not welcome are issues or PRs that suggest what might be called "personal taste" suggestions: add new or change value of an existing config option, add new plugin, etc. For that please use [Discussions](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/discussions).

Great job! As a new neovim user i found this very useful! 😄 
Maybe, for less experienced users like me, a shorter delay in `mini.clue` would help

> Great job! As a new neovim user i found this very useful! 😄 Maybe, for less experienced users like me, a shorter delay in `mini.clue` would help

Thanks for kind words! The delay is 'mini.clue' default and is described in the MiniMax's comment. It is deliberately not small to not result in a flicker when using keys that have clues.

The delay can be customized via [`config.window.delay`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-clue.html#miniclue.config-window) if you feel like a lower value can be more useful for you. In MiniMax 'plugin/30_mini.lua' it is a matter of adding an extra line inside `setup()` call (after all the `triggers` table) like `window = { delay = 500 },`.

Hello @echasnovski, I have been using MiniMax for a while with surprisingly little amount of issues. Recently I have face one when creating my own base16 theme using mini.base16.

As suggests, my theme uses mini.base16 and initializes `base00..base0F`. The problem is with `base05` which means the foreground colors. For some reason, it colors variables, functions, braces and more. This wasn't supposed to happend as there are separate base for those colors. The problem only happens with C++ files. I have installed the C++ parser from nvim-treesitter and is active.

Thanks.

Hey, what do you mean "*surprisingly* little amount of issues"? 😠 (Just joking :) )

> As suggests, my theme uses mini.base16 and initializes `base00..base0F`. The problem is with `base05` which means the foreground colors. For some reason, it colors variables, functions, braces and more. This wasn't supposed to happend as there are separate base for those colors. The problem only happens with C++ files. I have installed the C++ parser from nvim-treesitter and is active.

The 'mini.base16' is a fairly low-effort port of [chriskempson/base16-vim](https://github.com/chriskempson/base16-vim). It does define all built-in (a.k.a. "legacy"; like `Constant`, `Function`, etc.; see `:h group-names`) syntax highlighting groups, but does not adjust a lot of the "new" syntax highlight groups (like `@constant`, `@function.cpp`, etc.; see `:h treesitter-highlight-groups`).

The new groups should already be covered by their default linking to legacy groups, but it might look not the best in some languages.

My suggestion is to basically "learn to fish" here and adjust 'mini.base16' result as you see fit:
- Put cursor on the word that you want to highlight differently.
- Execute `:Inspect`. It will show all the highlight groups that are "active" at cursor, their values or links, and how they look. They are usually combined from top to bottom: lower group "overrides" attributes from the higher group and all attributes are combined.
- See the tree-sitter or LSP based group name for the `cpp` language. It might be something like `@function.call.cpp` - i.e. the `@function.call` group that is applied only for the `cpp` tree-sitter parser.
- Add something like `vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, '@function.call.cpp', { fg = p.base0D })` (assuming you have `local p = { ... }` as a palette) *after* applying 'mini.base16' highlighting.

Hope this helps. Also, a small heads up - 'mini.base16' is not *quite* as polished as 'mini.hues'. Mostly because the main goal is to follow "official" base16 style with as small maintenance as possible. My suggestion for MiniMax users is to use 'mini.hues' or some other third-party color schemes.
@echasnovski, will any improvement to tree-sitter's "new" highlighting be brought to mini.base16 to make it *consistent* in different languages? Thanks.

> [@echasnovski](https://github.com/echasnovski), will any improvement to tree-sitter's "new" highlighting be brought to mini.base16 to make it _consistent_ in different languages? Thanks.

It is already consistent in a sense that it always (for all languages) uses default links and doesn't tweak language specific groups. Similar goes for 'mini.hues', but to a lesser extent.

If you have concrete examples of the problems you have in cpp, I can help you with a concrete examples. For that, create a dedicated discussion in 'mini.nvim', please.

> _SOLUTION:_ Sorry to [@echasnovski](https://github.com/echasnovski) for all the hassle he had to bear. It was indeed a very silly mistake by me. Mainly, I had to add `cpp` to the `ensure_installed` variable inside the `nvim-treesitter` configuration. That has solved the issue. I should have realized the bug earlier as there is clearly a loop trying to highlight every filetype from `ensured_installed` list. Closing. Thanks.

No worries, it's great that you figured it out. Welcome to Neovim :)

(Note: on latest `main` it is just `languages` now instead of `ensure_installed`; specifically to draw attention that these are not just for ensuring installation but to also enabling).

One thing I would like to adjust is have all the keymaps starting with `<C-w>` to be also available starting with `<leader>w`, 
it there an easy way to that I can put that in my config?

i tried this:
`vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>w', '<C-w>', { noremap = false })`
and it works
but the clue does not show up
and adding 
`      { mode = 'n', keys = '<leader>w' },    -- Window commands`
to the `triggers` does not help

Thanks for kind words!

> One thing I would like to adjust is have all the keymaps starting with `<C-w>` to be also available starting with `<leader>w`,
> it there an easy way to that I can put that in my config?

The 'mini.clue' module needs to know about all available keys that can be followed by `<Leader>w`, as it does not know about them after a simple `<Leader>w -> <C-w>` remap. There are two ways to achieve that:
- Manually create custom mappings for all variants (like `<Leader>ws`, `<Leader>wv`, etc.) *with description*. Doable, but cumbersome.
- Only add clues for all these combinations. Luckily, 'mini.clue' provides a helper that generates such clues for `<C-w>`: [`MiniClue.gen_clues.windows()`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-clue.html#miniclue.gen_clues.windows), so they only require replacing `<C-w>` with `<Leader>w`. Here is the [comment that describes this solution](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2028#discussioncomment-14533695).

Was wondering if it was an easy to do, if you are using mini.starter, to have that display after the last buffer is closed. I am using sessions, so I can go to my parent folder where I keep all local repositories, and run nvim from there to be able to work on any repo I want from the sessions section. If I close out all buffers instead of sitting there with an empty one, it'd be cool to go back to mini.starter so I can pick another repo. Not an urgent or big deal as I could just open mini.file and go from there..

> ... if you are using mini.starter, to have that display after the last buffer is closed.

Should be possible in one way or another by creating an autocommand for `BufDelete` event. But the main problem here is to translate "last buffer is closed" into code, because Neovim always has at least one listed buffer present.

One approach that can be useful is to define a "good buffer" as a normal+listed+named buffer. Then the following autocommand should do the trick:

```lua
local is_good_buf = function(buf_id)
  local is_normal = vim.bo[buf_id].buftype == ''
  local is_listed = vim.fn.buflisted(buf_id) == 1
  local is_named = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(buf_id) ~= ''
  return is_normal and is_listed and is_named
end

-- Use `schedule_wrap` to execute *after* buffer is deleted
local show_starter_after_last_good_buf = vim.schedule_wrap(function()
  for _, buf_id in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
    if is_good_buf(buf_id) then return end
  end
  MiniStarter.open()
end)

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('BufDelete', { callback = show_starter_after_last_good_buf })
```

In MiniMax the last autocomman creation can be like this:

```lua
_G.Config.new_autocmd('BufDelete', '*', show_starter_after_last_good_buf, 'Show starter after last buffer')
```

Hello.I’m new to Neovim and might be missing something.

I noticed that when starting Neovim with `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-minimax nvim file.lua`,`lua_ls` is not attached. Following the documentation, I uncomment LSP and Mason, and then installed `lua-language-server`
via `:Mason`. 
```
now_if_args(function()
  add('neovim/nvim-lspconfig')

  -- Use `:h vim.lsp.enable()` to automatically enable language server based on
  -- the rules provided by 'nvim-lspconfig'.
  -- Use `:h vim.lsp.config()` or 'after/lsp/' directory to configure servers.
  -- Uncomment and tweak the following `vim.lsp.enable()` call to enable servers.
  vim.lsp.enable({
    -- For example, if `lua-language-server` is installed, use `'lua_ls'` entry
    'lua_ls'
  })
end)

later(function()
  add('mason-org/mason.nvim')
  require('mason').setup()
end)

```

It works correctly when the file is opened after startup(like `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-minimax nvim` and then press `<Leader>ei`).

> I noticed that when starting Neovim with `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-minimax nvim file.lua`,`lua_ls` is not attached. Following the documentation, I uncomment LSP and Mason, and then installed `lua-language-server`
> via `:Mason`.

Thanks for noticing! It was indeed a MiniMax problem since `now_if_args` is needed for 'mason.nvim' also. It should be enabled before Neovim tries to attach LSP server to the initial (argument) file(s).

This example should now [be fixed](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/7a920d245044a4b71186edf992aa9dc77b2545b6/configs/nvim-0.11/plugin/40_plugins.lua#L145) on latest `main`.

Hi @echasnovski , thank you for setting this config up for a layman like me. Migrating from nvim-kickstart. I have succesfully set it up in archlinux on wsl and found it had a little lag when pressing the leader key and waiting for the other key options  and as well as when using it. Is there any further tweaks which I need to do to refine the experience. I am also waiting eagerly  waiting for the setup for nvim 0.12.
I loved the default colorscheme is it Kanazawa or something you have made for this this setup. If so can we use it elsewhere

Thanks for kind words!

> ... little lag when pressing the leader key and waiting for the other key options and as well as when using it.

If you mean about a one second delay before the 'mini.clue' window appears in the bottom right, then it is just a delay for showing the clues. It should be possible to press something like `<Space>ei` with almost zero delay between key presses for the mapping to act (open 'init.lua' file in this case).

> I loved the default colorscheme is it Kanazawa or something you have made for this this setup. If so can we use it elsewhere

[It is 'miniwinter'](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/a9f0ae15269f40f52c7126ed97abd82d71e0924b/configs/nvim-0.11/plugin/30_mini.lua#L37). It is [part of 'mini.nvim'](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/7e55c3d2c04da134085a31156196836f80a89982/colors/miniwinter.lua). It does not have any precompute configs to be used outside of Neovim, but the palette is fully present in the linked file. Some extra work required to adapt for other applications, I am afraid.

> then it is just a delay for showing the clues

@Trid-collab In case it was not obvious, that delay is [configurable](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-clue.html#miniclue.config).

Public testing period for MiniMax in general is long overdue to be finished. Which it is now, since overall structure and documentation style seems to work fine in `nvim-0.11` reference config.

Thank you all for taking part in discussions!
